clue.text: Make a fool of one going on a mystery trip perhaps

definitions.meaning: to trick or deceive someone, to con them

definitions.text: going on a mystery trip perhaps
definitions.meaning: literally, carrying someone along on a journey, such as a coach outing with an unknown destination

explanation.surface: Someone tricks a person who has signed up for a coach outing to an unknown destination.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to swindle or dupe, while its literal reading is giving someone a lift on an excursion.

clue.text: Flatly it carries afternoon refreshments

parts.note: a flat object used for bearing cups, pot and cakes when the afternoon brew is served

explanation.surface: A deadpan remark that something bears the afternoon snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flatly' sounds like a manner of speaking, but it describes the shape of the thing doing the carrying.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat serving board is used to bring cups and a pot to the table at teatime.

clue.text: King again goes a short distance in Russian building

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
RE is a prefix meaning again

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a mile is a measure of distance
taken as written

explanation.surface: A monarch walks a little way once more inside a Moscow edifice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts the last letter from MILE, leaving MIL.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moscow citadel housing the Russian government is the famous fortified complex of that name.

clue.text: Figure out a way to obtain protection in the home

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the word before it are worked out into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: Advice to devise a method for keeping a household safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges FIGURE into FIREGU.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen placed in front of an open hearth guards a household against sparks and burns.

clue.text: Somewhat more lethargically offered room for rent again

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone sluggishly put up lodgings to let once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To let again means leasing out accommodation a second time to a new tenant.

clue.text: Most of the army unit's diet

indicators.note: most of means all but the final letter of the word is used

parts.note: a regiment is an army unit

explanation.surface: What a body of soldiers mostly eats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' drops the final T of REGIMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A prescribed course of food and exercise is a synonym for a diet.

clue.text: Drew with no real object in mind

definitions.text: Drew with no real object in mind

parts.words: Drew with no real object in mind
parts.note: made idle aimless sketches while thinking of something else

explanation.surface: An artist sketched without any purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Scribbling absent-mindedly in a margin is exactly this sort of aimless drawing.

clue.text: Inventive painter found in the studio

definitions.text: Inventive painter found in the studio

parts.words: Inventive painter found in the studio
parts.note: a person who paints faces with cosmetics for film or television, and whose first part also means invented

explanation.surface: A creative artist works in their atelier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'studio' suggests an artist's workshop, but it is a film or TV studio, and 'Inventive' plays on 'make up' meaning invent.
explanation.definitionFit: Studio staff who apply cosmetics to performers literally paint faces, and to make up a story is to invent it.

clue.text: Sportsman of a mature disposition

indicators.note: disposition, as an arrangement of parts, says the letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: An athlete with a grown-up temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' looks like temperament, but it signals rearranging A MATURE.
explanation.definitionFit: An unpaid sportsman who plays for love rather than money is a non-professional.

clue.text: Drag the wretched person used as bait

parts.note: to lug is to drag or haul
a worm is a contemptible, wretched person

explanation.surface: Someone hauls a miserable wretch along to use as a lure.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: a creature used as bait.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishermen dig these sandy marine creatures to put on hooks as fishing lures.

clue.text: Give false account of reformed miser here

indicators.note: reformed, as in formed again, says the letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

parts.note: present means here, in attendance

explanation.surface: Someone tells lies about a skinflint who has mended his ways and is now in attendance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' rearranges MISER into MISRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To misrepresent is to describe something falsely or misleadingly.

clue.text: But it does not stop the listener from receiving a radio communication

definitions.text: But it does not stop the listener from receiving a radio communication

parts.words: But it does not stop the listener from receiving a radio communication
parts.note: a stopper for the hearing organ, which still lets a plug, a radio advertisement, be spoken about

explanation.surface: A complaint that some device fails to keep a radio audience from hearing a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the device keeps sound out but its second half, a 'plug', is itself a radio promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft stopper worn in the ear blocks out noise, and a plug is a broadcast advertisement.

clue.text: Must topless Zulu dance about on an old burial mound?

indicators.note: to dance about is to move around wildly, so the letters are jumbled
topless means the word loses its first letter, as a down-style head

explanation.surface: A Zulu warrior with no shirt must perform a dance on an ancient grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' drops the Z of ZULU, leaving ULU; 'dance about' rearranges MUST with ULU.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrow, an earthen heap raised over an ancient grave, is the archaeologist's word for it.

clue.text: Youth leader in agony to make a lodgment

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: pain is agony

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A gang's young head suffers greatly while trying to bank money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Youth leader' gives Y, the first letter of 'Youth', which goes inside PAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To deposit money in a bank account is to lodge it; lodgment is an old word for deposit.

clue.text: Nervous with everybody above a precipice

parts.note: all means everybody
on can mean on top of, above
the edge of a cliff is a precipice

explanation.surface: Everyone is jittery standing at the top of a cliff.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tense and jumpy is the meaning of this idiom.

clue.text: Prominent position of tree is not important

parts.note: the lime or linden is a tree
light means trivial or unimportant, as in light reading

explanation.surface: A tree's location is of no great matter.
explanation.definitionFit: The centre of public attention is named after old stage lighting that made performers stand out.

clue.text: Conduct of rogues or Clara with mods rioting

indicators.note: rioting suggests wild disorder, so the letters are thrown into confusion

explanation.surface: Roguish behaviour from a girl and her gang of 1960s youths in a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: Mods were 1960s British youth gangs on scooters, famous for seaside riots; 'rioting' rearranges CLARA and MODS.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -dom names a realm or state, so this is the collective behaviour of scoundrels.

clue.text: Ringleader comes in to arouse support

indicators.note: comes in says this letter enters the other piece

parts.note: to stir up is to arouse
the leader, first letter, of 'ring' is R

explanation.surface: The chief troublemaker arrives to incite a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ringleader' looks like a mob boss but gives R, the first letter of 'ring'.
explanation.definitionFit: The loop hanging from a saddle supports a rider's foot.

clue.text: From Vigo Ann went to a French city

indicators.note: went, in the sense of moved off or turned, shows the letters shifting into a new order

explanation.surface: Ann travelled from the Spanish port of Vigo to a city in France.
explanation.walkthrough: Vigo is a Spanish port, setting the travel scene; 'went' rearranges VIGO ANN.
explanation.definitionFit: This city in Provence on the Rhône was the seat of the popes in the fourteenth century.

clue.text: In which one is mistaken

parts.note: the state of being wrong, as when one is said to be 'in' it

explanation.surface: A description of a situation where someone has got it wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: One is said to be 'in' this state when wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistake is something one can be 'in', wrongly believing something.

clue.text: Show zeal then thus, especially within

indicators.note: within says the answer is lodged inside the run of words

explanation.surface: An odd instruction pointing to something in particular, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from 'thEN' through 'THUS' into 'Especially'.
explanation.definitionFit: To gush or express eager excitement is to display enthusiasm.

clue.text: Knock sailor coming up at last repeated

indicators.note: last says this piece comes at the end
coming up, in a down entry, means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

indicators.note: repeated means the word is given twice over

explanation.surface: A seaman arrives with a knock that is repeated at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns TAR into RAT; 'repeated' doubles AT to give ATAT, placed 'last'.
explanation.definitionFit: The sound of repeated rapping on a door imitates a knocking noise.

clue.text: First to sign

definitions.meaning: to mark a document with the letters of one's name

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means earliest or opening, and the verb means writing one's capital letters as a signature.

clue.text: Loamy deposit confused Leo on a steamer

indicators.note: confused says the letters of the name are muddled

parts.note: SS is steamship, a steamer

explanation.surface: A muddled man named Leo aboard a ship near some silt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges LEO into LOE.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine windblown silt laid down as fertile yellowish soil is a geological term.

clue.text: Is to let out it was not an overstatement

indicators.note: out, as in put out of order, signals that the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that letting something slip was no exaggeration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let out' looks like a phrase, but 'let' is part of the anagram and 'out' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This rhetorical figure is understatement, such as 'not bad' for very good.

clue.text: Boy, recent modification 'e completed

indicators.note: completed says this piece finishes off the word
modification means a change, so the letters are altered in order

parts.note: the dropped-aitch 'e is taken as the letter E

explanation.surface: A lad says a recent change has been finished by him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modification' rearranges RECENT into TERENC; 'completed' puts E at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A male first name stands in for a boy, as is common in crosswords.

clue.text: Excess weight of one who overeats

parts.note: a glut is an excess or surplus
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Extra heaviness carried by a big eater.
explanation.definitionFit: A greedy person who consumes too much food is a gourmand.

clue.text: Within one's range of interest-not far from home

definitions.meaning: suited to one's tastes or abilities
literally, on the road where one lives

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means suited to one's liking, while its literal reading is the road where one lives.
